sourceLabel: ProofWiki, Square Root of 2 is Irrational
evidence: Read Proof 5: applies the Rational Root Theorem to n^2-2, numerator divides 2 and denominator divides 1, candidates +-1,+-2 checked to fail. Rational Root Theorem itself is cited, not reproved, as in the sketch.

sourceLabel: C. Erickson, Prime Numbers and the Riemann Hypothesis (Pitt)
preciseLocator: Section 2, The Riemann Zeta Function and the Primes (Euler product, Theorem 5)
evidence: Read it: derives the Euler product from unique factorization, then takes s->1+ and says the limit diverges because the harmonic series does, concluding infinitely many primes. Missing: the integral-comparison divergence step and an explicit 'finite product stays bounded' step (only implicit).
sketchProblem: Sketch says it overlaps route 3-r2 and is not distinct unless developed separately; arXiv 1202.3670 (current ref) only lists proofs and does not write this one out.

evidence: Read arXiv 1202.3670 sec 3.2 (survey, no worked proof of this route), Conrad 'Euclidean proofs of Dirichlet's theorem' (only lists polynomials h(T) and Schur/Murty theorems), MIT 18.781 lecture 12 (cyclotomic only). No free source found proving a generic aN+1 product route.
sketchProblem: Sketch is incoherent: 'a N+1' with generic a cannot force q = a mod m, and it admits as much. It is not a single provable route; a real Euclid-style proof needs a specific polynomial per progression (e.g. 4p1...pk-1 for 3 mod 4). Suggest rewriting around a concrete case or merging with 4-r2.

sourceLabel: MIT OCW 18.781 Theory of Numbers, Lecture 12
evidence: Read the full text: Phi_n integral, monic, constant term 1 (Prop 45); no common root mod p with x^m-1 for m|n proper, p not dividing n (Lemma 46); Theorem 47 takes Phi_n(l n p1...pN), a prime divisor has order exactly n so n | p-1, giving a new prime = 1 mod n.
sketchProblem: Source proves only 1 mod n, matching sketch. Slight variant: it uses a = l n p1...pN with l large rather than 'choose A to exclude exceptional divisors'.

evidence: Opened Conrad 'Euclidean proofs of Dirichlet's theorem' (kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/gradnumthy/dirichleteuclid.pdf): Theorems 1-2 (Schur, Murty) say Euclid-style polynomials exist for a mod m iff a^2=1 mod m, which supports the scope remark but is not the claimed statement; did not read the Springer book proof.
sketchProblem: Route is a scope warning, not a proof route; there is nothing to verify as a complete proof. Suggest flagging not-a-route. The statement about L-function nonvanishing is true but is not what Conrad's text proves.

sourceLabel: Edgar and Trevino, Many proofs that 1+2+...+n = n(n+1)/2
evidence: Read: S=1+...+n, reversed S=n+...+1, adding gives 2S=n(n+1). Exactly the sketch. Also Wikipedia Arithmetic progression, Sum > Derivation, gives the general reverse-and-add.

sourceLabel: Edgar and Trevino, Many proofs that 1+2+...+n = n(n+1)/2
evidence: Read: counts 2-subsets of {1,...,n+1} as C(n+1,2) and by larger element b as sum (b-1)=1+...+n. Same double-counting idea, but on strict pairs of n+1 objects, not pairs i<=j on n or multisets; the identification of i<=j pairs with C(n+1,2) is not written. Same proof in discrete.openmathbooks.org/dmoi2/sec_comb-proofs.html, exercise 3.
sketchProblem: Sketch's 'choosing two with repetition gives n(n+1)/2' is asserted without justification; it needs the shift (i,j)->(i,j+1).

sourceLabel: Edgar and Trevino, Many proofs that 1+2+...+n = n(n+1)/2
evidence: Read: differentiates sum x^k = (1-x^{n+1})/(1-x), gets sum k x^{k-1} = (n x^{n+1}-(n+1)x^n+1)/(1-x)^2, takes x->1 with L'Hospital to get n(n+1)/2. Matches the sketch.
sketchProblem: Sketch's S(x)=1+x+...+x^n is right; derivative at 1 needs the limit step, which the source supplies.

preciseLocator: Section on gnomons of square numbers (the n-square to (n+1)-square paragraph)
evidence: Read: going from n-square to (n+1)-square adds 2n+1 elements (one per row, one per column, one corner), and states this gnomonic technique proves the sum of the first n odd numbers is n^2. Short, but all steps present. Wikipedia Square number only has pictures.
sketchProblem: Source indexes the border as 2n+1 (n -> n+1); sketch's nth border 2n-1 is the same up to shift.

evidence: Read ProofWiki Odd Number Theorem (induction and arithmetic-sum proofs only), Wikipedia Galileo's law of odd numbers (algebraic via AP sum), Wikipedia Square number (picture), Edgar-Trevino (telescopes (k+1)^2-k^2 to sum 1..n, not the odd-sum). No source found telescoping k^2-(k-1)^2=2k-1 to get n^2.
Read: expands (x+y)^n by distributivity into 2^n products, groups by number k of y's, counts k-element subsets of the n factors as C(n,k). Matches the sketch. OpenStax 11.6 does not print this.

evidence: Read: distributive expansion into 2^n products e1...en with ei in {x,y}, rearranged to x^{n-k}y^k, count of those equals number of k-subsets C(n,k). Matches sketch step for step.
